name: Example corporate playbook: buying services
note: An invented baseline for demonstration. A real one comes from the company's legal team.

rules.title: Payment terms
rules.standard: Undisputed invoices are payable 30 days or more after receipt. We may withhold amounts disputed in good faith.
rules.red_flags: Payment due in under 30 days; late interest above 1% per month; no right to dispute or withhold; payment in advance.

rules.title: Fees and price changes
rules.standard: Fees are fixed for the term or change only by written agreement; any annual increase is capped (CPI or 5%).
rules.red_flags: Provider may raise fees unilaterally or pass through costs without a cap or our approval.

rules.title: Limitation of liability
rules.standard: Mutual cap of at least the fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months. No cap for gross negligence, wilful misconduct, breach of confidentiality or indemnity obligations.
rules.red_flags: Cap below 12 months of fees; cap that protects only the provider; provider liable only for gross negligence or wilful misconduct; our liability uncapped.

rules.title: Consequential damages
rules.standard: Mutual waiver of indirect and consequential damages, with the same carve-outs as the liability cap.
rules.red_flags: One-sided waiver that protects only the provider.

rules.title: Indemnification
rules.standard: Mutual indemnities for third-party claims caused by breach, negligence or misconduct. Provider indemnifies us for IP infringement by the services.
rules.red_flags: We indemnify the provider broadly while the provider gives no indemnity; indemnity for the provider's own negligence.

rules.title: Service standard and warranties
rules.standard: Services are performed with reasonable skill and care, to at least the standard the provider uses for its own business, and in compliance with law.
rules.red_flags: All warranties disclaimed with no service standard; services provided 'as is'.

rules.title: Termination rights
rules.standard: We may terminate any service for convenience on 60 days' notice or less. Either party may terminate for material breach after a 30-day cure period.
rules.red_flags: No termination for convenience for us; notice longer than 90 days; provider may terminate without cause on short notice; termination fees.

rules.title: Term and renewal
rules.standard: Fixed initial term. Renewal only by written agreement, or automatic renewal of at most one year with a right to opt out.
rules.red_flags: Automatic multi-year renewal; opt-out window that is easy to miss.

rules.title: Confidentiality
rules.standard: Mutual obligations with the usual exceptions (public, already known, independently developed, legally required), lasting at least 3 years after termination.
rules.red_flags: Obligations on us only; shorter than 3 years; no exception for disclosure required by law.

rules.title: Data protection and security
rules.standard: Provider protects our data with reasonable safeguards and notifies us promptly (within 72 hours) of a security breach affecting it.
rules.red_flags: No security obligation; no duty to notify of a breach; provider may use our data for its own purposes.

rules.title: Intellectual property
rules.standard: Each party keeps what it owned before. We own, or receive a perpetual licence to, deliverables created for us.
rules.red_flags: Provider owns everything created for us and grants no licence that outlives the agreement.

rules.title: Governing law and venue
rules.standard: Delaware or New York law, with courts in the same state.
rules.red_flags: Another US state is a medium risk. Law or venue outside the United States is a high risk. Mandatory arbitration in the provider's home city.

rules.title: Assignment and subcontracting
rules.standard: No assignment without the other party's written consent, except to an affiliate or a successor to the business. The provider stays responsible for its subcontractors.
rules.red_flags: Provider may assign or subcontract freely; we may not assign even to an affiliate.

rules.title: Records and audit
rules.standard: Provider keeps accurate records of the services and charges, and we may audit them on reasonable notice at least once a year.
rules.red_flags: No audit right; audit only at our cost with long notice; records kept for less than 3 years.

rules.title: Force majeure
rules.standard: Mutual relief for events beyond reasonable control, a duty to mitigate, and a right to terminate the affected service if the event lasts more than 60 days. Payment obligations for services already received are not excused.
rules.red_flags: Relief for the provider only; no termination right for a prolonged event.
